chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr from Muhammad ibn Umar al-Sabati who said:

I asked al-Rida (peace be upon him) about a man who married a woman and divorced her before consummating the marriage. He said, 'There is no waiting period (iddah) for her.' And I asked him about a woman whose husband died before consummating the marriage. He said, 'There is no waiting period for her; the two cases are equal.'

key_terms.الرِّضَا: Al-Rida (title of Imam Musa al-Kadhim or Imam Ali al-Rida, contextually referring to the Imam being asked)
key_terms.السَّابَاطِيُّ: Al-Sabati (a specific tribal or geographic identifier for the narrator Muhammad ibn Umar)

ai.seo_question: What is the iddah (waiting period) for a woman divorced or widowed before marital consummation?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) clarifies that in both pre-consummation divorce and pre-consummation widowhood, the woman is exempt from the waiting period (iddah), establishing their legal equivalence. This ruling is derived from the principle that the primary purpose of iddah in these contexts is to ascertain potential pregnancy, which is less certain or relevant before consummation. The narration underscores the precision of Shia jurisprudence in distinguishing between the effects of divorce and death on marital status prior to the full realization of the marital bond.
